corpora.name: human-mc4-web
corpora.what: 2,000 random pages of the German-language web (.de 1,215, .com 346, .at 104, .ch 87, other 248): the prose paragraphs of each page (12 or more words, enough function words, at most 45% capitalised words because German capitalises nouns; scripts/lib/prose.mjs), 40 to 1,200 words, spam keywords excluded, drawn by a seeded shuffle (seed 42) by scripts/sample-mc4-web.mjs. A check against ordinary prose of every kind; the German entries were chosen on it.
corpora.license: ODC-BY 1.0 for mC4, plus Common Crawl terms; the page text belongs to each site, so only URL, date, shard and SHA-256 are shipped.
corpora.caveats: Web pages, not personal mail or essays. mC4 drops lines without end punctuation, so headings, bullets, subject lines and hashtag-only lines are mostly missing and the structure entries cannot be tested well on it.

corpora.name: human-mc4-web-holdout
corpora.what: 1,000 further pages from the same shuffle, kept back while the German entries were chosen and measured once at the end.
corpora.license: ODC-BY 1.0 for mC4, plus Common Crawl terms; the page text belongs to each site, so only URL, date, shard and SHA-256 are shipped.

corpora.name: human-mc4-news
corpora.what: 814 pages from German, Austrian and Swiss news sites (99 hosts, among them derstandard.at, welt.de, tagesspiegel.de, handelsblatt.com, rp-online.de, spiegel.de, nzz.ch, zeit.de and regional papers): every qualifying page in the shard whose host matched a list of news sites. Same prose filter as human-mc4-web. News stands in for edited general prose.
corpora.license: ODC-BY 1.0 for mC4, plus Common Crawl terms; the page text belongs to each site, so only URL, date, shard and SHA-256 are shipped.
corpora.caveats: The host list also caught a few portals and tech sites (t-online.de, heise.de, golem.de). Some pages are reader comments under articles.

corpora.name: human-mc4-shop
corpora.what: 370 German-language pages whose URL path contains /produkt/, /produkte/, /product/, /products/, /shop/, /onlineshop/, /webshop/, /item/, /artikeldetail(s)/ or /p/ (293 hosts; otto.de 18, buecher.de 8, galaxus.ch 7, orellfuessli.ch 7), with eBay, Amazon, Etsy, AliExpress, DHgate, Wish, Tripadvisor, Agoda, Booking and a few non-shop sites excluded. Same prose filter as human-mc4-web: the text is the page's prose paragraphs, product descriptions and shop copy among them.
corpora.license: ODC-BY 1.0 for mC4, plus Common Crawl terms; the page text belongs to each site, so only URL, date, shard and SHA-256 are shipped.
corpora.caveats: Filtered by URL only and not checked by hand: besides product descriptions it holds publisher blurbs from book shops, trade-fair and manufacturer pages, a forum and a few coupon pages. No cap per host, so large shops appear several times. German product copy in general, not Etsy or print-on-demand.

corpora.name: human-mc4-shop-holdout
corpora.what: 367 pages chosen by the same URL filter from another validation shard, kept back while the entries were chosen and measured once at the end.
corpora.license: ODC-BY 1.0 for mC4, plus Common Crawl terms; the page text belongs to each site, so only URL, date, shard and SHA-256 are shipped.
corpora.caveats: As human-mc4-shop. 50 of its 291 hosts also appear in human-mc4-shop, so it is not independent by host.

corpora.name: ai-general
corpora.what: Claude Sonnet (48) and Claude Haiku (48) answering plain German requests in six genres (blog post, email to colleagues, short essay, newspaper article, LinkedIn post, short report) on eight everyday topics, made by scripts/generate-general.mjs from scripts/general-requests.json. The models saw no pattern list. The German entries were drawn from this set, so its hit rates overstate recall; ai-multi-holdout and ai-detailed-holdout are the clean held-out measure.
corpora.caveats: Anthropic models only, 96 texts. Each row records the resolved model id and the system prompt, which tells the model to ignore any name or email address in its context. One reply (email-5-sonnet) contained the account owner's name; it was discarded and requested again, and the row records that (discarded: 1).

corpora.name: ai-general-holdout
corpora.what: Claude Sonnet (48) and Claude Haiku (48) answering the German requests in scripts/general-requests-holdout.json: the same six genres as ai-general, eight new topics. Generated together with ai-general. Its results were read during the 0.3.0 review rounds, so it is no longer a clean held-out estimate; ai-multi-holdout and ai-detailed-holdout are.
corpora.caveats: Anthropic models only, 96 texts. No reply was discarded.

corpora.name: ai-multi-holdout
corpora.what: Six models answering plain one-line requests from scripts/multi-requests.json: seven genres (blog post, email to friends, short essay, local newspaper article, Instagram post, short report, and a long article of about 800 words) on eight everyday topics that appear in no other corpus. Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5), Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5) and Claude Sonnet 4.5 (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) answered all 56 requests each (224 texts). OpenAI GPT-5.5 (gpt-5.5-2026-04-23) answered the six short genres on the first topic (6 texts) and GPT-5.4 mini (gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17) the six short genres on the first four topics (24 texts). Sent through the OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages APIs by scripts/generate-api.mjs with no system prompt, default sampling and a 16,000 token limit: the models saw only the request and never a pattern list. Each row records the generator, provider, resolved model id, the exact request and the stop reason. Made after the lists of this release were final, never used to choose or tune an entry, and measured once.
corpora.caveats: OpenAI is kept small for budget: 30 of 254 texts, two models, no long form, so the GPT rows show direction only. Every reply ended normally (stop or end_turn) and is at least 200 characters long. The Claude rows were checked for the right language, personal data, refusals and duplicates. Email addresses, web addresses and phone numbers that could belong to a real person or business were replaced after generation with example.* addresses and placeholder numbers, in the requests and in the replies alike.

corpora.name: ai-detailed-holdout
corpora.what: Realistic requests with concrete facts, as people type them to a chat assistant: 56 scenarios (eight per genre, the same seven genres as ai-multi-holdout, outlined in scripts/detailed-scenarios.md), each written twice in the language, as a short request (style A, one or two sentences) and a careful one (style B, with audience, tone, length and the facts as notes), in scripts/detailed-requests/de.json. Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5), Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5) and Claude Sonnet 4.5 (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) answered all 112 requests each, through the Anthropic Message Batches API (scripts/generate-api.mjs batch) with no system prompt, default sampling and a 16,000 token limit. Most scenarios are set in Germany (336 texts), the rest in Austria (56) and Switzerland (56); each row carries the variety. Each row records the generator, resolved model id, style, scenario, the exact request and the stop reason. Made after the lists of this release were final, never used to choose or tune an entry, and measured once.
corpora.caveats: Anthropic models only. The requests were written for this study by a model that did not see the pattern lists, following the scenario outline; names, places, addresses and contact details in them are invented. Every reply ended with end_turn and was checked for the right language, personal data, refusals and duplicates. Email addresses, web addresses and phone numbers that could belong to a real person or business were replaced after generation with example.* addresses and placeholder numbers, in the requests and in the replies alike.

notUsed: No independent machine-written German product copy was available, so no product-only entry could be backed by machine evidence and the German list has none.
The em dash, English curly quotes and guillemets were measured and are not entries: the models used none of them, while human German pages use them often (see skill-notes.md).
